pages.text: Pocket peeks out of the backpack. Yellow taxis hum down the street, beep, beep. "Hello, New York," says Pocket. Look and look.
Rumble, rumble, whoosh! The subway train sweeps into the station. Pocket hops onto a seat and holds on tight.
Pocket sits on a bench in Central Park. The trees are green and the path is wide. "Hello, New York," says Pocket. Look and look.
Round and round goes the carousel. Up and down go the painted horses, white and red and gold.
Coo, coo! Four grey pigeons bob along the path, pecking and strutting. Bob, bob, bob go their little heads.
Pocket sniffs a warm, salty pretzel from the cart. Twisty and brown. "Hello, New York," says Pocket. Look and look.
The ferry sails across the harbour, splash, splash. There is the Statue of Liberty, tall and green, holding up her torch.
The Brooklyn Bridge stretches across the water, arch after arch. The sky glows orange. "Hello, New York," says Pocket. Look and look.
The Empire State Building stands tall as the sun goes down. Its windows glow pink and gold, up and up and up.
Back at the hotel, the sky turns soft lavender. One by one, the lights come on. "Hello, New York," says Pocket. Look and look.
The lights twinkle. Pocket yawns a big, slow yawn. One ear droops. Then the other.
Pocket is tucked up in the hotel room, fast asleep. Goodnight, Pocket. Goodnight, New York.
